chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about coitus interruptus, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is up to the man'.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Who has the authority to decide on coitus interruptus in Islam?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of 'al-'azl' (coitus interruptus) is primarily the husband's prerogative, reflecting the juristic view that it does not require the wife's explicit consent unless it causes her harm. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the balance of rights within marriage, particularly regarding contraception and the prevention of pregnancy without severing the marital bond.
